questions.subject: PERSONAL_FINANCE
questions.learningObjective: Apply home and renters insurance concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: A practical case: Andres Novak receives $1,220 of monthly income and spends $244 on transportation. What percentage of income is that?

options.misconception: divides the whole by the part instead of the part by the whole
forgets to multiply the fraction by one hundred
reports the dollar amount rather than the percentage share

questions.explanation: The share is the part divided by the whole, then multiplied by one hundred. $244 divided by $1,220 is 0.2 as a decimal, so 20% of income goes to transportation. Dividing the other way or skipping the factor of one hundred gives a different, wrong figure.
questions.hint: Divide the expense by income, then convert to a percent.

provenance.author: bank-team-personal-finance
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: PERSONAL_FINANCE
questions.learningObjective: Apply home and renters insurance concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: Think it over: A homeowners policy costs $276 per year. What is the equivalent monthly premium?

options.misconception: uses a weekly conversion instead of monthly
quotes the yearly cost as if it were monthly
multiplies rather than divides the annual cost

questions.explanation: A yearly premium spread evenly over twelve months is $23. Quoting the annual figure, dividing by fifty-two, or multiplying by twelve does not give the monthly amount owed.
questions.hint: Divide the annual premium by twelve.

questions.subject: PERSONAL_FINANCE
questions.learningObjective: Apply home and renters insurance concepts to realistic financial decisions
questions.stem: Here is the case: A homeowners policy has a $600 deductible and a $24,200 limit. A covered loss of $35,600 occurs. How much does the insurer pay?

options.misconception: ignores the deductible
subtracts only half of the deductible
pays the full loss without applying either term

questions.explanation: The insurer pays the smaller of the loss and the policy limit, then subtracts the deductible. That is $23,600 here. Ignoring the limit or the deductible, or paying the whole loss, misstates the claim settlement.
questions.hint: Apply the limit first, then subtract the deductible.
